# #003. Profit-to-Cost Ratio & Charnes-Cooper

<!-- section:scenario -->
A specialty manufacturer chooses continuous output levels $x_i \in [0, \text{capacities}[i]]$ across $n$ product lines. Unlike standard profit maximization, management evaluates performance by **efficiency ratio** — net return divided by total resource spend:

$$
\max_x \; \frac{\text{baseRevenue} + \sum_i \text{revenues}[i] \, x_i}{\text{baseCost} + \sum_i \text{costs}[i] \, x_i}
$$

Total production must fall within `minTotal <= sum(x) <= maxTotal`, and a sustainability policy mandates that line `greenIndex` accounts for at least `minGreenShare` of total output (`x[greenIndex] >= minGreenShare * sum(x)`).

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P003Input`)**:
  - `baseRevenue: number`, `baseCost: number` — fixed numerator/denominator offsets (`baseCost + sum(costs[i]*x[i]) > 0`)
  - `revenues: number[]`, `costs: number[]` — marginal revenue and cost per unit of line $i$
  - `capacities: number[]` — per-line upper bounds on $x_i$
  - `minTotal: number`, `maxTotal: number` — lower/upper bounds on total output $\sum_i x_i$
  - `greenIndex: number`, `minGreenShare: number` — minimum share required for the designated green line
- **Output (`P003Output`)**:
  - `quantities: number[]` — optimal production vector $x$
  - `ratio: number` — maximum achievable objective ratio

<!-- section:example -->
With `baseRevenue = -60`, `baseCost = 15`, `revenues = [20, 15, 22]`, `costs = [8, 10, 12]`, `capacities = [30, 30, 20]`, `minTotal = 20`, `maxTotal = 50`, `greenIndex = 1`, `minGreenShare = 0.25`:

- Simply maximizing unit efficiency `revenue[i]/cost[i]` ignores the negative fixed offset `baseRevenue = -60` and the `25%` green-line rule.
- Solving the Charnes-Cooper LP yields `quantities = [30, 10, 0]`, giving numerator `(-60 + 600 + 150) = 690` and denominator `(15 + 240 + 100) = 355`, ratio **`690 / 355 ≈ 1.94366`**.

<!-- section:hint1 -->
You cannot divide decision variables by decision variables inside an LP solver! Instead, set $t = \frac{1}{\text{baseCost} + \sum_i c_i x_i} > 0$ and introduce homogenized variables $y_i = t \cdot x_i \ge 0$. Notice what becomes of the denominator when multiplied by $t$!

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Under $(t, y)$ where $t > 0$ and $y_i \ge 0$:
1. The denominator equation becomes **`baseCost * t + dot(costs, y) == 1`**.
2. The objective becomes **`maximize baseRevenue * t + dot(revenues, y)`**.
3. Multiply every constraint's constants by `t`: `y[i] <= capacities[i] * t`, `minTotal * t <= sum(y) <= maxTotal * t`, and `y[greenIndex] >= minGreenShare * sum(y)` (homogenous!).
4. After solving, recover **`quantities[i] = y[i] / t`**!

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\max_{y \ge 0, \, t \ge 0} \quad & r_0 t + \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} r_i y_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & c_0 t + \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} c_i y_i = 1 \\
& y_i \le U_i t && \forall i \\
& L_{\text{tot}} t \le \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} y_i \le U_{\text{tot}} t \\
& y_{\text{green}} \ge \alpha \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} y_i
\end{aligned}
$$

Because $c_0 + \sum c_i x_i > 0$ across the bounded feasible polytope, $t^* > 0$ strictly at optimum, making the mapping $x_i = y_i / t$ an exact bijection!

judge.m0: Output must be an object { quantities, ratio }.
judge.m4: Green line share ({p0}%) is below minimum ({p1}%).
judge.m5: Denominator cost ({p0}) must be strictly positive.
judge.m6: Reported ratio ({p0}) does not match computed revenue/cost ({p1}).
judge.m7: Feasible schedule, but ratio ({p0}) is below optimal ({p1}).
